verdicts_so_far.stage2: H2 (coupling degree) MIXED: C2, C3 pass; C1, C4 fail
verdicts_so_far.stage3: P1 FAIL, P2 FAIL; P3 PQK non-inferior to RBF-SVM in 9/9 task x N cells

builds_on.design_note: Stage 4 was designed after Stages 1-3 to test whether their conclusions are specific to the ZZ re-uploading map. Stage 1-3 verdicts are not revisited. All Stage 4 hypotheses, thresholds and the analysis code are fixed by this file before any Stage 4 result on real data exists.

families.havlicek_zz: H; R_z(2 c x_k); ZZ(2 (pi - c x_i)(pi - c x_j))
families.iqp: H; R_z(c x_k); ZZ(c^2 x_i x_j)
families.xy: R_y(c x_k); exp(-i t (XX+YY)/2), t = c^2 x_i x_j
families.heisenberg: R_y(c x_k); exp(-i t (XX+YY+ZZ)/2), t = c^2 x_i x_j
families.ms_xx: R_y(c x_k); exp(-i t XX/2), t = c^2 x_i x_j
families.hea_cnot: R_y(c x_k) R_z(c x_k); CNOT(i -> j)
families.cz_layers: R_y(c x_k) R_z(c x_k); CZ(i, j)
families.crx: R_y(c x_k); CRX(c x_i), control i, target j
families.separable: R_y(c x_k) R_z(c x_k); no two-qubit gates

circuit_conventions: L layers; each layer = single-qubit encoding gates then two-qubit gates on the sorted edge list; R_a(t) = exp(-i t A/2); qubit q receives feature q (importance order); exact statevector simulation; Bloch vectors (X, Y, Z expectations) of every qubit are the projected-kernel features
cone_definition: light cone measured from the circuit: D(k) = {j : shifting x_j by 1.0 changes qubit k's Bloch vector by more than 1e-13 (max over 24 Gaussian inputs, seed 7, c = 1.0)}; computed per family, graph, n and L. Checks: inside the backward gate-walk bound; equal to the graph-distance-L cone for zz_reupload; no sensitivity value in the ambiguous band [1e-14, 1e-12).
concentration_measure: V_k = trace of the covariance (across inputs) of qubit k's Bloch vector

partA.graphs_note: the Stage 2 graph generator with seed 20261001; graphs that do not exist at a given n, or duplicate another graph's edge set, are skipped
partA.fresh_rows: 200 training rows per dataset drawn with seed 20261001+4, excluding every row used in Stages 1 and 2

partB.separable_family: graph ignored: run once per (L, c) as graph 'empty'
partB.validation_subset: as Stage 3: stratified 2000 rows of the validation split, seed 0
partB.test_subset: as Stage 3: stratified min(4000, all) rows of the clean test split, seed 20261001; the same rows for every model
partB.quantum_kernel: as Stage 3: projected 1-RDM kernel, gamma = multiplier / median distance (500 training points), multipliers {0.5, 1, 2}, SVM C in {1, 10, 100}, class_weight balanced, tuned on validation with the seed-0 sample, refit per seed
partB.comparators: as Stage 3: RBF-SVM and the Phase 0 best classical model on identical training samples and test rows
partB.selection: 'validation-selected' = highest validation macro-F1 among the stated configurations; ties broken by the order graph list -> L -> c

hypotheses.A1: Degree mechanism generalises. For each entangling family, in every cell (inputs, c, n, heterogeneous graph, L in {2,3}) compute the Spearman correlation between coupling degree d_k and V_k across qubits; the family passes if >= 80% of its cells are negative (undefined correlations count as not negative). GENERALISES if >= 7 of the 9 entangling families pass; FAMILY-SPECIFIC if 3-6 pass; DOES NOT GENERALISE if <= 2 pass.
hypotheses.A2: Cone irrelevance at equal degree generalises. For each entangling family, compare graphs with equal uniform degree (same n, L, c, inputs) whose mean light cone differs by >= 0.5: median |log(V_larger_cone / V_smaller_cone)| (V averaged over qubits). The family passes if it has >= 10 such pairs, the median is <= 0.05, and the median is <= one third of the family's median one-step degree effect (matching -> ring, ring -> regular3, same n, L, c, inputs). Same 7 / 3-6 / <= 2 rule.
hypotheses.A3: Descriptive (no pass/fail): per family, R2 of log V_k on [d_k, L, d_k*L] versus [|D(k)|, L, |D(k)|*L], per (inputs, c).
hypotheses.B1: Concentration does not predict accuracy (replicates Stage 3 P1 failure). For each family and task at N = 1000, Spearman correlation across that family's configurations (graph, L, c) between mean V (seed-0 training sample) and seed-averaged test macro-F1. Concentration is predictive for a family if the correlation is positive with p < 0.05 in >= 2 of 3 tasks. B1 REPLICATES if concentration is not predictive in >= 8 of the 10 families.
hypotheses.B2: Entanglement adds no meaningful accuracy (replicates Stage 3 entangled-vs-uncoupled). For each entangling family, task and N: delta = seed-averaged test macro-F1 of the family's validation-selected coupled configuration (graph != empty) minus that of its validation-selected uncoupled configuration (graph = empty; same gates without two-qubit gates). B2 REPLICATES if delta <= +0.02 in >= 80% of the 81 cells.
hypotheses.B3: Non-inferiority to RBF-SVM (replicates Stage 3 P3). For each family, task and N: the family's validation-selected configuration versus RBF-SVM, paired bootstrap 95% CI (1000 resamples of test rows, seed-0 predictions) of the macro-F1 difference; non-inferior if the lower bound is > -0.01. B3 REPLICATES if non-inferior in >= 80% of the 90 cells.
hypotheses.B4: Bandwidth matters more than graph (replicates Stage 3). For each entangling family and task at N = 1000: bandwidth effect = mean over (graph, L) of the range of seed-averaged macro-F1 across c; graph effect = mean over (L, c) of the range across graphs. B4 REPLICATES if the bandwidth effect exceeds the graph effect in >= 18 of the 27 cells.

decision.stage3_generalises: B1, B2 and B3 all replicate -> 'Stage 3 conclusions GENERALISE across the ten families'; one or two replicate -> 'PARTLY GENERALISE'; none -> 'DO NOT GENERALISE'. B4 reported alongside.
decision.concentration_mechanism: A1 and A2 reported with their three-level outcome
decision.verification: if any circuit check fails, nothing is interpreted
decision.reproduction: zz_reupload configurations that also appear in Stage 3 are compared with the Stage 3 results (reported, not a hypothesis)
